findings.title: SpanFlusher.join can leave remaining flusher processes running after timeout
findings.body: When `deadline` is not None and `remaining_time <= 0`, the loop breaks before calling `process.terminate()` on any later processes. Since `self.next_step.join(timeout)` may consume the entire timeout, this commonly skips all flusher processes. If a process is hung and does not observe `self.stopped`, it is never terminated, so old flusher processes can continue flushing and producing Kafka messages after the consumer has moved on. The timeout path should continue terminating all processes even after the deadline expires instead of breaking out of the loop.

findings.title: Negative --flusher-processes crashes SpanFlusher initialization
findings.body: The new `--flusher-processes` option is accepted as any int and `SpanFlusher` does not validate that `max_processes` is positive. If a negative value is supplied, `self.num_processes` becomes negative, so `range(self.num_processes)` is empty and `process_to_shards_map` has no keys. The shard distribution loop then computes `process_index = i % self.num_processes` and indexes the empty map, raising `KeyError` and preventing the consumer from starting. Add `click.IntRange(min=1)` or an explicit constructor check.

findings.title: record_stored_segments is called on unused per-flusher buffers
findings.body: `submit()` now calls `buffer.record_stored_segments()` on each `SpansBuffer` in `self.buffers`. Those buffers are created by `_create_process_for_shards` for the flusher processes and are never passed to `process_batch`/`process_spans`; spans are actually written through the original ingest-side buffer created in `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.create_with_partitions`. The previous code recorded on that ingest-side buffer. Any segment counters or state accumulated by `process_spans` are no longer recorded, so stored-segment metrics can silently underreport or zero out.

findings.title: New flusher_processes parameter inserted before produce_to_pipe breaks positional callers
findings.body: `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.__init__` now has `flusher_processes` as the sixth positional argument with `produce_to_pipe` seventh. Any existing caller that passed `produce_to_pipe` as the sixth positional argument will now bind that callable to `flusher_processes` and leave `produce_to_pipe` as `None`, silently disabling the pipe/test path or causing type/value errors. `SpanFlusher.__init__` has the same issue with `max_processes`. Prefer keyword-only for the new parameters or append them after existing parameters.
